prompts.title: Long Shadow
prompts.brief: Find a shadow that is longer or stranger than the thing casting it, and make the shadow the subject of the frame.

prompts.title: Window Light
prompts.brief: Let one window decide the lighting. Show how its light lands on a wall, a floor or an object nearby.

prompts.title: Clean Silhouette
prompts.brief: Shoot toward the light so an object becomes a flat dark shape. Keep its outline simple enough to recognise at a glance.

prompts.title: Converging Lines
prompts.brief: Frame straight lines that meet, repeat or cross. Stand square to the scene and keep the verticals upright.

prompts.title: Circle Hunt
prompts.brief: Find a circle nobody meant you to admire, like a drain, a lid or a ring of rust, and let it fill the frame.

prompts.title: Stair Rhythm
prompts.brief: Use steps, ramps or railings to build a beat of repeated shapes that pulls the eye through the picture.

prompts.title: Rough Meets Smooth
prompts.brief: Put a rough surface beside a smooth one in the same frame so the contrast can almost be felt through the screen.

prompts.title: Wearing Away
prompts.brief: Get close to a surface that is slowly giving way: flaking paint, cracked mud, polished stone. Show its grain.

prompts.title: Soft to the Eye
prompts.brief: Find something that looks soft to the touch, such as wool, moss, rising dough or folded linen, and make us want to feel it.

prompts.title: Puddle World
prompts.brief: Use a puddle, wet pavement or still pond to show a second scene, upside down, beneath the first.

prompts.title: Curved Mirror
prompts.brief: Capture a scene bent by a spoon, a kettle, a bowl or a glass sphere. The bend should be what we notice first.

prompts.title: Glass Layers
prompts.brief: Let a window show what is outside and what is reflected at the same time, and make the two layers work together.

prompts.title: Tiny Giant
prompts.brief: Make something very small look enormous, or something huge look small, using only your angle and your distance.

prompts.title: Small in Big Space
prompts.brief: Place one tiny subject in a wide empty setting so that the space around it tells the story.

prompts.title: Close Enough to Count
prompts.brief: Move in until you can count the parts: petals, bricks, stitches, grains of sand. Keep the nearest detail sharp.

prompts.title: Nobody Home
prompts.brief: Show a place that looks as if people just left: a pulled-out chair, a lit lamp, a half-finished puzzle. No people in frame.

prompts.title: Quiet Place
prompts.brief: Photograph a street, hall or stairwell at a moment when nobody is there, and let the emptiness set the mood.

prompts.title: Traces Left Behind
prompts.brief: Show the evidence that someone passed by, like footprints, a cup ring or a worn path, without showing anyone.

prompts.title: Waiting Objects
prompts.brief: Photograph an object that seems to be waiting for its owner: a bike against a wall, a coat on a hook, shoes by a door.

prompts.title: One Colour Only
prompts.brief: Fill the frame with a single colour in several shades. Look for it in walls, fabric, food or leaves.

prompts.title: Colour Clash
prompts.brief: Find two colours that should not work together, then frame them so that they somehow do.

prompts.title: One Bright Spot
prompts.brief: Keep the scene calm and muted, and let one small spot of bright colour take all of the attention.

prompts.title: Blur on Purpose
prompts.brief: Turn movement into streaks with a slow shutter or a steady pan, while one part of the scene stays sharp.

prompts.title: Frozen Moment
prompts.brief: Freeze something that is normally too quick to see: poured water, drifting flour, a splash, a spinning top.

prompts.title: Wind at Work
prompts.brief: Show the wind without showing the wind: bending grass, a snapping flag, tumbling leaves or a billowing curtain.

prompts.title: New Angle on the Old
prompts.brief: Take one familiar object and photograph it from an angle nobody uses, until it looks like a landscape or a creature.

prompts.title: Accidental Face
prompts.brief: Find a face in something that is not a face: a socket, a tap, a pair of windows. Frame it so the expression is clear.

prompts.title: Laid Out Neatly
prompts.brief: Arrange ordinary things like keys, buttons or pegs into a tidy pattern and photograph it straight from above.

prompts.title: Tool Portrait
prompts.brief: Treat a well-used tool or utensil like a portrait subject: soft light, a plain background, and its history showing.

prompts.title: Overlooked
prompts.brief: Photograph something you pass every day without noticing, and show it so that others see it properly for the first time.
